approvalStatus: Endorsed by the Coptic Orthodox Church; witnessed by crowds of multiple faiths

en.name: Our Lady of Zeitoun
en.summary: Prolonged series of apparitions over a Coptic Orthodox church in Cairo, witnessed by enormous crowds of Christians, Muslims, and others across several years.
en.body: Beginning in April 1968, workers near a Coptic Orthodox church in the Zeitoun district of Cairo, Egypt, reported seeing a luminous figure resembling the Virgin Mary appear repeatedly above the church's domes, a phenomenon that continued intermittently for several years and was eventually witnessed, according to contemporary reports, by crowds sometimes estimated in the hundreds of thousands, including Christians of multiple denominations, Muslims, and people of no particular faith, with sightings reported by Egyptian government officials, journalists, and even the country's president at the time. Unlike most Marian apparitions, no single visionary received private messages; the phenomenon was instead a widely and publicly visible luminous appearance, often accompanied by figures resembling doves of light, that was extensively photographed and investigated by both religious and secular authorities without a conclusive natural explanation being established. The event was formally endorsed as a genuine apparition by the Coptic Orthodox Church, and it remains one of the most widely witnessed reported Marian phenomena of the modern era, drawing veneration across multiple Christian traditions.
